summary: DCR Transmission, L.L.C. files tariff revisions under section 205 on November 16, 2026, in ER27-512-000, answering the CAISO show cause order. It owns the Ten West Link, a 125-mile 500 kV line, and adds a new Appendix IV with large load interconnection procedures, a pro forma agreement modeled on CAISO's generator agreement, and an interim service. It adds no new transmission service.

points.point: DCR is a single-asset owner whose line crosses the California-Arizona border.
points.quote: DCRT owns and operates the 125-mile, 500 kilovolt Ten West Link Transmission Line

points.point: It notes the other parties held other views but tailors its filing to its position as a single-asset owner.
points.quote: tailored its proposed tariff revisions to its unique situation as a single-asset PTO whose transmission line traverses the California-Arizona border

points.point: It proposes no new transmission service, deferring to CAISO.
points.quote: DCRT has not proposed additional or revised transmission services in this filing

points.point: Its study steps average about 85 days, within the 60 to 90 day range FERC set.
points.quote: these steps will average roughly 85 calendar days from start to finish, meeting the OSC Order’s target of 60–90 days

points.point: Its pro forma large load interconnection agreement is modeled on CAISO's generator agreement.
points.quote: generally modeled on the CAISO’s pro forma Large Generator Interconnection Agreement (“LGIA”)

points.point: Co-located generation that exports must still go through CAISO's generator process.
points.quote: Any generating facility that will export energy to the CAISO Controlled Grid, however, must interconnect through the CAISO’s GIDAP and execute a Commission-accepted LGIA

points.point: The interim service lasts until the identified upgrades reach commercial operation.
points.quote: a Large Load Interconnection Customer may elect to take FILI Service until the Network Upgrades identified in Appendix A have achieved Commercial Operation

points.point: Large load facilities are reimbursed for upgrades over $10 million once they reach commercial operation.
points.quote: Large Load Facilities will be reimbursed for Reimbursable Network Upgrades costing more than $10 million if the Large Load Facility reaches commercial operation

throughLine.text: Filed under section 205 to answer the E-10 show cause order. It adds a study process, an interconnection agreement and an interim service, handles cost responsibility through reimbursement terms, and leaves new transmission services to CAISO.
